about: Synthetic research notes for development, tests and demo mode (P12-T05). Every note is fictional and labelled DEMO, is about a fictional DEMO instrument or a fictional market, and is not a recommendation. Figures in the notes are illustrative.

items.title: DEMO note: Demo Global Equity ETF holdings spread
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Global Equity ETF tracks a fictional index of large companies across many countries and sectors. Its spread lowers single-company risk, but it still falls with global equity markets. Currency moves against the US dollar change its value for investors who report in shillings or dirhams.

items.title: DEMO note: costs of the Demo Global Equity ETF
items.summary: DEMO research. The fund's illustrative expense ratio is 0.20% a year. Trading spreads and platform fees are extra and differ by broker. Past index returns are not a guide to future returns.

items.title: DEMO note: concentration in the Demo Technology ETF
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Technology ETF holds a narrow set of technology companies, so a few holdings drive most of its movement. It has been more volatile than broad equity funds and can fall sharply when technology shares fall.

items.title: DEMO note: interest-rate risk in the Demo Global Bond ETF
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Global Bond ETF holds fictional government and corporate bonds. When interest rates rise, bond prices fall, and the fund's value falls with them. Its income can change as the bonds it holds are replaced.

items.title: DEMO note: what the Demo Gold Tracker ETF does and does not do
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Gold Tracker follows a fictional gold price. Gold pays no income and its price can move a lot over months. Some investors hold it to diversify, but it has also fallen in periods when shares rose.

items.title: DEMO note: volatility and custody risk of Demo Bitcoin
items.summary: DEMO research. Demo Bitcoin is a fictional crypto asset. Crypto prices can rise or fall by large amounts in days. Custody, exchange failure and regulatory changes are additional risks, and rules differ between Kenya and the UAE.

items.title: DEMO note: Demo Kenya Telecom dividends and regulation
items.summary: DEMO research. Demo Kenya Telecom is a fictional listed telecom company. Its dividends depend on profits and can be cut. Licence conditions, tax changes and competition in mobile money are the main risks named in its fictional reports.

items.title: DEMO note: credit cycle risk for Demo Kenya Bank
items.summary: DEMO research. Demo Kenya Bank is a fictional bank. Bank shares are sensitive to loan defaults and interest-rate changes. A rise in bad loans would reduce profits and could reduce dividends.

items.title: DEMO note: occupancy and rent in the Demo Nairobi Income REIT
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Nairobi Income REIT owns fictional offices and shops. Its distributions depend on occupancy and rents. Vacancies, rent arrears and property revaluations can lower both its income and its price.

items.title: DEMO note: holding the Demo Kenya Treasury Bond 2030 to maturity
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Kenya Treasury Bond 2030 is a fictional shilling government bond. Its price changes with interest rates before maturity. Selling before 2030 can give a different result from holding it to maturity.

items.title: DEMO note: yields and access in the Demo Shilling Money Market Fund
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Shilling Money Market Fund invests in fictional short-term deposits and bills. Its yield changes with short-term interest rates. Money is usually available within days, but the fund is not a bank deposit.

items.title: DEMO note: early withdrawal from the Demo Shilling 12-Month Fixed Deposit
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Shilling Fixed Deposit locks money for 12 months. Withdrawing early may cost the interest earned. The rate is fixed at the start, so it does not rise if market rates rise.

items.title: DEMO note: property cycle exposure of Demo Gulf Developer
items.summary: DEMO research. Demo Gulf Developer is a fictional property developer. Its profits follow property sales, which move with interest rates and demand. A slowdown in sales would hit both earnings and the share price.

items.title: DEMO note: structure of the Demo Dirham Sukuk 2029
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Dirham Sukuk is a fictional Sharia-compliant certificate. Payments depend on the issuer and the underlying assets. Its price changes with interest rates, and it can be hard to sell quickly.

items.title: DEMO note: liquidity of the Demo Dubai Rental Property Share
items.summary: DEMO research. The Demo Dubai Rental Property Share is a fictional fractional property holding. Selling can take months, valuations are infrequent and rental income can stop when units are empty.

items.title: DEMO note: shilling and dirham exchange-rate risk
items.summary: DEMO research. For an investor who reports in shillings or dirhams, holdings in other currencies change in value when exchange rates move. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar in this fictional market; the shilling floats.
